s0101.literal: Only in seizing land north of the Huai did he not adopt Xi's plan; Wu Mingche in the end was defeated. Emperor Xuan deeply regretted it and said to Yuan Xian: "Had I not used Mao Xi's plan, matters would never have come to this—it is my fault."
s0101.idiomatic: Only in seizing land north of the Huai did he not take Xi's advice; Wu Mingche was defeated in the end. Emperor Xuan deeply regretted it and told Yuan Xian, "Had I followed Mao Xi's plan, this would not have happened—it is my fault."

s0102.literal: As Xi grew still closer, he spoke without holding back. Yet the heir apparent was fond of wine and revelry; every night he held long feasts with his favorites. Xi often spoke on it; Emperor Xuan used this to warn the heir, who secretly resented him; by then he was somewhat estranged.
s0102.idiomatic: As Xi grew closer still, he spoke without reserve. Yet the heir apparent loved wine and nightly revels with his favorites. Xi often remonstrated; Emperor Xuan used this to warn the heir, who secretly resented him and by then had grown somewhat distant.

s0103.literal: Earlier, Houzhu had been wounded by the Prince of Shixing; when his sores healed he celebrated by himself, set wine in the rear hall, summoned Jiang Zong and others below, spread music and composed verse, and when drunk summoned Xi.
s0103.idiomatic: Earlier Houzhu had been wounded by the Prince of Shixing. When his wounds healed he celebrated alone, set wine in the rear hall, summoned Jiang Zong and others, spread music and composed verse, and when drunk called for Xi.

s0104.literal: At that time the imperial tomb had only just been completed and not yet a full year had passed. Xi, displeased at seeing this, wished to remonstrate but Houzhu was already drunk. Xi mounted the steps, feigned heart illness, fell on the steps below, and was moved out of the Secretariat.
s0104.idiomatic: The imperial tomb had only just been completed and a full year had not yet passed. Xi was displeased and wished to remonstrate, but Houzhu was already drunk. Xi mounted the steps, feigned heart trouble, collapsed on the steps, and was carried out of the secretariat.

s0105.literal: When Houzhu woke he grew suspicious and said to Jiang Zong: "I regret summoning Mao Xi. I know he has no illness—he only wished to block my merry feast. That is not what I would do; he is deceitful."
s0105.idiomatic: When Houzhu woke he grew suspicious and said to Jiang Zong, "I regret calling Mao Xi. I know he is not ill—he only wanted to spoil my feast. That is not my way; he is deceitful."

s0106.literal: He then plotted with Sima Shen, saying: "This man is proud. I wish to hand him over to the Poyang brothers to let them take revenge—is that acceptable?"
s0106.idiomatic: He then plotted with Sima Shen and said, "This man is proud. I want to hand him to the Poyang brothers to let them take revenge—is that acceptable?"

s0107.literal: He replied: "In the end he will not serve the state. I wish it as Your Majesty commands."
s0107.idiomatic: He replied, "He will never serve the state again. I bow to Your Majesty's will."

s0108.literal: Fu Zai contested this, saying: "That will not do."
s0108.idiomatic: Fu Zai objected, "That will not do."

s0109.literal: If revenge is granted, where does that leave the late emperor?"
s0109.idiomatic: If you allow revenge, where does that leave the late emperor?"

s0110.literal: Houzhu said: "He shall be begged off to a small commandery and not allowed to see state affairs."
s0110.idiomatic: Houzhu said, "Give him a small commandery and keep him from court affairs."

s0111.literal: Xi was then made interior minister of Yongjia.
s0111.idiomatic: Xi was then made interior minister of Yongjia.

s0112.literal: When Xi reached the commandery he accepted no salary or stipend; his government was broad and quiet, and people and officials found it convenient.
s0112.idiomatic: When Xi reached the commandery he took no salary; his rule was open and quiet, and people and officials were well served.

s0113.literal: When Fengzhou inspector Zhang Dabao raised troops in rebellion, the commandery adjoined Fengzhou yet had never had defenses. Xi then repaired the city walls and ditches and strictly arrayed weapons.
s0113.idiomatic: When Fengzhou inspector Zhang Dabao rebelled, the commandery bordered Fengzhou but had never been defended. Xi repaired walls and ditches and arrayed weapons.

s0114.literal: He also sent his subordinate Songyang magistrate Zhou Pan leading a thousand troops to aid Jian'an.
s0114.idiomatic: He also sent his subordinate Songyang magistrate Zhou Pan with a thousand men to relieve Jian'an.

s0115.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was appointed interior minister of Nan'an.
s0115.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified he was made interior minister of Nan'an.

s0116.literal: In Zhenming year 1 he was summoned as grand master for splendid happiness and concurrently left valiant-cavalry general.
s0116.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 he was summoned as grand master for splendid happiness and left valiant-cavalry general.

s0117.literal: Xi had benevolent administration in the commandery; when he was summoned to court, those who escorted him on the road extended for several hundred li.
s0117.idiomatic: Xi had ruled with kindness; when he was recalled to court, escorts followed him for hundreds of li.

s0118.literal: That year he died of illness on the road, aged seventy-two.
s0118.idiomatic: That year he died of illness on the road, aged seventy-two.

s0119.literal: He left a collected works in ten scrolls.
s0119.idiomatic: He left collected works in ten scrolls.

s0120.literal: His son Chuchong succeeded him and rose to aide on the staff equal in ceremony to the Three Dukes and gentleman attendant of the Secretariat.
s0120.idiomatic: His son Chuchong succeeded him and rose to aide on a staff equal in ceremony to the Three Dukes and gentleman attendant of the secretariat.

s0121.literal: Cai Zheng, styled Xixiang, was son of attendant-in-ordinary and central pacifying-army general Cai Jingli.
s0121.idiomatic: Cai Zheng, styled Xixiang, was the son of attendant-in-ordinary and central pacifying-army general Cai Jingli.

s0122.literal: In youth he was clever and keen, with sharp discernment and strong memory.
s0122.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever, with sharp judgment and a strong memory.

s0123.literal: At age six he called on Liang's minister of the board of civil office, Chu Xiang of Henan; Xiang's style was Zhongju [4]; he marveled at his quick wit.
s0123.idiomatic: At six he visited Liang minister of the board of civil office Chu Xiang of Henan; Xiang's style was Zhongju [4], and he marveled at the boy's quick wit.

s0124.literal: At seven he mourned his mother and observed mourning like an adult's rites.
s0124.idiomatic: At seven he mourned his mother and observed mourning like an adult.

s0125.literal: His stepmother Lady Liu was fierce and jealous and did not treat him properly. Zheng served her all the more carefully and at first showed no resentment.
s0125.idiomatic: His stepmother Lady Liu was fierce and jealous and treated him harshly. Zheng served her all the more carefully and at first showed no resentment.

s0126.literal: Zheng's original name was Lan; Jingli thought he had Wang Xiang's nature, renamed him Zheng, and styled him Xixiang.
s0126.idiomatic: Zheng's original name was Lan. Jingli thought he had Wang Xiang's nature, renamed him Zheng, and styled him Xixiang.

s0127.literal: At the beginning of Liang's Chengsheng era the Founder was inspector of South Xuzhou, summoned him to fill the post of reception chief clerk, and soon made him erudite of the National University.
s0127.idiomatic: At the start of Liang's Chengsheng era the Founder was inspector of South Xuzhou, summoned him as reception chief clerk, and soon made him erudite of the National University.

s0128.literal: In the beginning of Tianjia he was moved to acting legal-cadre staff officer in the Prince of Shixing's household; he served through outside-troops staff officer and master of guests in the masters of writing, and wherever he was stationed he was praised for able administration.
s0128.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjia he became acting legal-cadre staff officer in the Prince of Shixing's household, then outside-troops staff officer and master of guests in the masters of writing; wherever he served he was praised for able administration.

s0129.literal: In the beginning of Taijian he was moved to aide in the heir apparent's junior tutor's office, steward of the Prince of Xin'an, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry on direct communication, registrar in the Prince of Jin'an's household, heir-apparent palace attendant, and concurrently leader of straight service in the eastern palace; palace attendant as before.
s0129.idiomatic: At the start of Taijian he was aide in the heir apparent's junior tutor's office, steward of the Prince of Xin'an, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry on direct communication, registrar in the Prince of Jin'an's household, heir-apparent palace attendant, and concurrently head of straight service in the eastern palace; palace attendant as before.

s0130.literal: He left office to mourn his father; when mourning ended he inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Xinfeng and was appointed sagely-dawn general and advising officer on the staff of the right-pacifying Prince of Xin'an.
s0130.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father; when mourning ended he inherited as Marquis of Xinfeng and was made sagely-dawn general and advising officer on the staff of the right-pacifying Prince of Xin'an.

s0131.literal: In Zhide year 2 he was moved to director of the Court of Judicial Review; soon he was minister-of-personnel vice director.
s0131.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he became director of the Court of Judicial Review, then vice director of the ministry of personnel.

s0132.literal: He was moved to heir-apparent aide and secretariat attendant, in charge of edicts and proclamations.
s0132.idiomatic: He was made heir-apparent aide and secretariat attendant, in charge of edicts.

s0133.literal: Soon he was made minister of the left household and, with vice director Jiang Zong, directed compilation of the five rites.
s0133.idiomatic: Soon he was minister of the left household and, with vice director Jiang Zong, directed compilation of the five rites.

s0134.literal: Soon he was additionally made pacifying-far general.
s0134.idiomatic: Soon he was also made pacifying-far general.

s0135.literal: Houzhu valued his ability; trust in him grew daily. He was moved to minister of personnel and secure-the-right general; every ten days he went once to the eastern palace and before the heir discoursed on gain and loss in past and present and on current government affairs.
s0135.idiomatic: Houzhu valued his talent and relied on him more each day. He was made minister of personnel and secure-the-right general; every ten days he went to the eastern palace and before the heir discussed gain and loss in history and current affairs.

s0136.literal: An edict also ordered that in the Court of Judicial Review's prison, matters great and small were to be decided on Zheng's deliberation.
s0136.idiomatic: An edict also ordered that in the Court of Judicial Review's prison, all cases great and small were to be decided on Zheng's advice.

s0137.literal: Soon an edict sent Zheng to recruit soldiers and form his own command; Zheng was good at comfort and care and won popular feeling; within a month his following neared ten thousand.
s0137.idiomatic: Soon an edict sent Zheng to recruit soldiers for his own command. He was good at comfort and won hearts; within a month his force neared ten thousand.

s0138.literal: Zheng's position and reputation were already weighty, and combined with his blazing influence; public opinion all feared and envied him.
s0138.idiomatic: Zheng's rank and fame were already great, and his influence blazed; opinion feared and resented him.

s0139.literal: Soon he was transferred to secretariat director; general as before.
s0139.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to secretariat director; his generalship was unchanged.

s0140.literal: The secretariat director's post was pure and simple with little business; some said Zheng had words of complaint; when it reached Houzhu he was greatly angry, seized his men and horses, and was about to execute him; those who firmly remonstrated won his pardon.
s0140.idiomatic: The secretariat director's post was pure and light; some said Zheng had complained. When Houzhu heard, he was furious, seized his men and horses, and was about to kill him; only firm remonstrance saved him.

s0141.literal: In Zhenming year 3 the Sui army crossed the river; Houzhu, because Zheng had practical ability, had him provisionally direct the central army supervisor's office.
s0141.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 the Sui army crossed the Yangzi. Houzhu, trusting Zheng's ability, had him provisionally direct the central army supervisor's office.

s0142.literal: Zheng toiled day and night with full exertion of heart and strength. Houzhu praised him and said, "When affairs are settled I shall repay you."
s0142.idiomatic: Zheng labored day and night with all his strength. Houzhu praised him and said, "When this is over I shall repay you."

s0143.literal: At the decisive battle on Zhongshan's southern ridge he was ordered to hold the great camp in the northwest of the palace city; soon he was told to supervise all armies in battle.
s0143.idiomatic: At the decisive battle on Zhongshan's southern ridge he was ordered to hold the great camp northwest of the palace city; soon he was told to supervise all armies in battle.

s0144.literal: When the city fell he entered the Pass in the usual way.
s0144.idiomatic: When the city fell he entered the Pass like the others.

s0145.literal: Zheng had fine looks and eloquence and investigated many subjects deeply.
s0145.idiomatic: Zheng was handsome and eloquent and had studied many fields deeply.

s0146.literal: As to gentry and official families, imperial clansmen, current institutions, statutes and ritual norms, household registers and customs, mountains and rivers and land—ask and he had no wrong answer.
s0146.idiomatic: On gentry and officials, imperial kin, current institutions, statutes and ritual, household registers and customs, mountains, rivers, and land—whatever one asked, he answered correctly.

s0147.literal: Yet by nature he was rather given to flattery and advancement and could not make modest retirement his calling.
s0147.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was given to flattery and advancement and could not rest in modest retirement.

s0148.literal: When he was first appointed minister of personnel he memorialized Houzhu to borrow ceremonial music escort. Houzhu told the responsible office: "Ceremonial music is military music, granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not measure himself and confuses our court regulations—yet since his father Jingli had merit in founding the state, it is fitting to grant as requested for now, but recall it immediately after the appointment ceremony."
s0148.idiomatic: When he was first made minister of personnel he asked Houzhu to lend him ceremonial music. Houzhu told the office, "Ceremonial music is military music, granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not know his place and confuses court rules—yet since his father Jingli helped found the state, grant it for now, but take it back as soon as the appointment rite is done."

s0149.literal: Zheng did not cultivate moral corners—all was of this kind.
s0149.idiomatic: Zheng did not keep his conduct clean—this was typical.

s0150.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his keen ability, summoned him for consultation, and his words always met the point—yet for many years he received no posting; after long delay he was made aide in the directorate of ceremonial affairs.
s0150.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his quick mind, summoned him for consultation, and his words always hit the mark—yet for years he received no post; after long delay he was made aide in the directorate of ceremonial affairs.

s0151.literal: He served through gentleman in the civil-affairs and ritual section of the masters of writing, was moved to supervisor-of-matters attendant [attendant], [5] and died, aged sixty-seven.
s0151.idiomatic: He served as gentleman in the civil-affairs and ritual section of the masters of writing, was moved to supervisor-of-matters attendant [attendant], [5] and died, aged sixty-seven.

s0152.literal: His son Yi studied the Documents and rose to clerk on the Three Dukes' staff and academician of virtuous instruction.
s0152.idiomatic: His son Yi studied the Documents and rose to clerk on the Three Dukes' staff and academician of virtuous instruction.

s0153.literal: Entering Sui he was an eastern-palace academician.
s0153.idiomatic: Under Sui he was an eastern-palace academician.

s0154.literal: The historiographer says: Zhuang Yuanrao from dawn to night never slackened, aiding affairs and benefiting the age.
s0154.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Zhuang Yuanrao never slackened from dawn to night, aiding affairs and benefiting the age.

s0155.literal: Sima Shen was pure and strict in court, toiling at hardship to establish conduct, and with loyal integrity added—beautiful indeed.
s0155.idiomatic: Sima Shen was pure and strict at court, toiling in hardship to establish his conduct; with loyal integrity added, he was admirable.

s0156.literal: Mao Xi deeply understood circumstances and aided the ruler of the age.
s0156.idiomatic: Mao Xi deeply understood circumstances and aided the ruler of his time.

s0157.literal: Cai Zheng was clever and talented in abundance, yet by seizing power he stumbled himself—pity.
s0157.idiomatic: Cai Zheng was clever and richly talented, yet by seizing power he tripped himself—a pity.

s0159.literal: [1] Once when he followed his father to call on the Minister of Personnel, Dao
s0159.idiomatic: [1] Once when he followed his father to call on the Minister of Personnel, Dao

s0161.idiomatic: On "[Gai]": emended per the Southern History.

s0162.literal: Comment: Dao Zhongju was the son of Dao Qia; see the biography of Dao Qia in the Book of Liang—he never served as minister of personnel.
s0162.idiomatic: Dao Zhongju was Dao Qia's son; see the Book of Liang biography of Dao Qia—he never served as minister of personnel.

s0163.literal: The biography of Dao Gai in the Book of Liang says Gai moved from interior minister of Jian'an to secretariat gentleman, concurrently minister of personnel.
s0163.idiomatic: The Book of Liang biography of Dao Gai says he moved from interior minister of Jian'an to secretariat gentleman, concurrently minister of personnel.

s0164.literal: It also says Emperor Wu of Liang played chess with him every time from evening until dawn.
s0164.idiomatic: It also says Emperor Wu of Liang played chess with him from evening until dawn.

s0165.literal: Thus "Dao Zhongju" is plainly an error for "Dao Gai."
s0165.idiomatic: Thus "Dao Zhongju" is plainly an error for "Dao Gai."

s0166.literal: [2] Then from his seat he called him to play—"play" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "play chess."
s0166.idiomatic: On "called him to play": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read play chess.

s0169.literal: [Zhao] county marquis—changed according to the biography in the patchwork Southern History.
s0169.idiomatic: On "[Zhao] county marquis": emended per the patchwork Southern History biography.

s0170.literal: The Hall edition Southern History also reads Shi.
s0170.idiomatic: The Hall edition Southern History also reads Shi.

s0171.literal: Zhang Yuanji's collation note says Zhao is correct.
s0171.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanji's collation note says Zhao is correct.

s0172.literal: In the Geography of Commanderies and Counties in the Book of Southern Qi, Wenzhao county belonged to Jin'kang commandery of Guangzhou.
s0172.idiomatic: The Book of Southern Qi, Geography of Commanderies and Counties, places Wenzhao county in Jin'kang commandery of Guangzhou.

s0174.literal: [4] Xiang's style Zhongju—the three characters "style Zhongju" are suspected as superfluous text.
s0174.idiomatic: On "Xiang's style Zhongju": the three words style Zhongju are probably superfluous.

s0175.literal: According to Chu Xiang's biography in the Book of Liang, his style was Shiju, not Zhongju.
s0175.idiomatic: Chu Xiang's Book of Liang biography gives his style as Shiju, not Zhongju.

s0176.literal: [5] Was moved to supervisor-of-matters [attendant]—supplemented according to the Southern History.
s0176.idiomatic: On "moved to supervisor-of-matters [attendant]": supplied per the Southern History.

s0177.literal: According to the Tongdian, Offices Canon, in Kaihuang year 6 of Sui an edict had the Ministry of Personnel establish the post of supervisor-of-matters attendant.
s0177.idiomatic: The Tongdian, Offices Canon, says that in Sui Kaihuang year 6 an edict had the ministry of personnel establish the post of supervisor-of-matters attendant.
